first_failures_preserved: Direct dependency downloads failed; resolved using the existing proxy and system CA, without disabling TLS verification.
Redis MSYS2 rejected C:/ config path; /cygdrive/c/ path and authenticated local runtime checks succeeded.
Initial SQL fixture omitted required funding columns; fixture corrected and six PostgreSQL tests passed.
Initial source import rejected historical orphan tombstones; now archives their hashes without restoring ownership.
Frontend TS6307 include boundary fixed; generated TS build files moved into ignored node_modules cache.
Initial HTTP test tried decoding PNG as JSON; binary handling fixed, separate retry report retained.

Independent review caught omitted Chat Completions cyber caller. First fixture falsely passed old code because usage marked a terminal frame. Corrected fixture reaches real partial/error path, old code submits two bills and fails; fixed code submits one and passes.
Browser first crashed/timed out; later local browser login/profile/relogin and subscription recovery succeeded. First browser failures retained.

First binary replacement encountered a Windows executable lock, so that smoke was explicitly excluded from rebuilt-binary acceptance. Process exit was awaited, SHA256 verified before starting the new binary. First bootstrap connection refusal retained; final 23 checks passed only after readiness.
not_accepted: Full browser/device/admin acceptance remains incomplete; browser acceptance is limited to synthetic username login, nickname edit, logout/relogin and native subscription failure/recovery. Model catalogue order is component-tested only.
Real upstream Codex/PDF/search/image/WS and interrupted-stream acceptance were not run for this single-core candidate.
Real ZPay merchant payment, callback, fulfillment and refund were not run.
Legacy scoped role10, pending payment callbacks, old response state, team management UI and purchase wiring remain integration gates.
Durable final-usage replay/crash reconciliation and WS per-turn funding remain release gates.
Cross-database final write barrier, authoritative cutover and rollback after new transactions were not implemented or rehearsed.
privacy: Only aggregate counts, hashes, protocol contracts and synthetic test outcomes are exported. Private DBs, account identities, key values, password hashes and raw runtime logs are excluded.
